_meta.purpose: Machine-readable checklist for skeptical layer-by-layer manual audit before release sealing. It guides human/agent eye review from upstream truth to downstream agent and release surfaces.
_meta.rule: Checklist items are not proof by themselves. They define where to look, which invariants to test, which evidence artifacts to compare, and which failure families to sweep when a defect is found.

global_invariants.question: Can this layer confuse SAGE source root, analyzed MAIN root, variation root, or external target root?
global_invariants.expected_signal: analysis_root, target_project, target_file and target_ref are explicit where the layer affects agent or repo decisions.

global_invariants.question: Does this layer prefer SQLite/source snapshots where available and label JSON as shadow/fallback instead of SSOT?
global_invariants.expected_signal: SQLite-first validators pass or the artifact declares why JSON/file content is the correct source.

global_invariants.question: If upstream truth changed, can this layer detect stale downstream artifacts and say so?
global_invariants.expected_signal: freshness, trust, snapshot hash, mtime/git, or proof debt status is visible.

global_invariants.question: Are file, symbol, line_start and line_end produced at the source of truth and preserved downstream?
global_invariants.expected_signal: Source-grounded spans match current source snapshots or clearly say unavailable/partial.

global_invariants.question: Does this layer keep MAIN edit context separate from variation/merge and external-target context?
global_invariants.expected_signal: Variation data appears only in merge/review surfaces unless explicitly requested.

global_invariants.question: Do doctrine, policy, principle, cage, capability and HITL decisions travel to consumers that rely on them?
global_invariants.expected_signal: Lineage/registry artifacts show produced and consumed decisions instead of hidden local duplication.

global_invariants.question: Does target-repo agent output avoid SAGE-internal implementation noise and provide actionable target-repo facts?
global_invariants.expected_signal: Agent packets contain target file/symbol/span/evidence/follow-up, not internal debug assumptions.

global_invariants.question: When this layer cannot know something, does it fail closed or speak with explicit unknown/fallback telemetry?
global_invariants.expected_signal: No silent exception, empty-success, or ambiguous PASS for missing evidence.

global_invariants.question: Does a positive-path validator exercise the declared authoritative source rather than succeeding only through a fallback or shadow representation?
global_invariants.expected_signal: Primary-path fixtures seed and verify authoritative truth; fallback behavior is tested separately and explicitly labeled as degraded evidence.

global_invariants.question: Do cross-artifact consumers derive PASS, FAIL and UNKNOWN through the canonical evidence-status contract across supported producer schemas?
global_invariants.expected_signal: No local partial status reader can turn valid evidence into false UNKNOWN or missing evidence into false PASS.

global_invariants.question: If this layer consumes another artifact, is ordering declared in a contract rather than remembered by the operator?
global_invariants.expected_signal: release_proof_steps_contract, pipeline execution contract, or profile policy declares the dependency.

global_invariants.question: Can this layer invalidate or require review for a human seal after relevant changes?
global_invariants.expected_signal: Seal impact policy or HITL artifact shows whether seal is current, review-required, or reseal-required.

global_invariants.question: Is any manual or agent-eye reviewed status derived only from automated PASS rather than a current review evidence record?
global_invariants.expected_signal: Manual review status requires an explicit reviewer record tied to the current packet fingerprint and source comparison; automated checks remain separately labeled.

global_invariants.question: Before closing this work package, did the operator check whether a reusable lesson, failure family, P1/P2 debt, or checklist update was discovered?
global_invariants.expected_signal: P0/P0.5 lessons are converted to guards/checklist entries when applicable; deferred P1/P2 items are recorded in the work item registry instead of chat context.

global_invariants.question: When a lesson is recorded, is the lesson written as a reusable failure-family rule rather than a one-off incident note?
global_invariants.expected_signal: The lesson/title/risk class describes the general class of failure; the concrete step, file or artifact remains in evidence/source fields unless the lesson is inherently one-off.

micro_walkthrough_policy.purpose: Define the extra skeptical questions used after macro layers and source layers when the audit walks pipeline steps, release-proof steps and artifact connectivity one item at a time.
micro_walkthrough_policy.rule: Micro walkthroughs must use existing registries as the order source. They must not create a second nervous system or duplicate pipeline/release/artifact truth.

scopes.sample_policy: Inspect the current pipeline step in registry order. Compare registry fields to source/orchestrator behavior and downstream artifacts before advancing the micro cursor.

checks.question: Do depends_on and execution ordering match actual upstream artifact needs?
checks.expected_signal: Required producers appear in depends_on or execution policy; no operator-memory ordering is needed.

checks.question: Do reads_artifacts and writes_artifacts match the real artifacts consumed and produced by the step?
checks.expected_signal: Pipeline registry, artifact provenance and source code agree on artifact IO.

checks.question: Is scheduler_class, sqlite_writer, heavy/full_only/profile guidance accurate for this step?
checks.expected_signal: Parallel/sequential/full-run behavior is declared and compatible with SQLite writes and generated artifact consumers.

checks.question: Can an operator or agent run the step through the canonical public command without relying on a private file path?
checks.expected_signal: canonical_step_command exists; direct-file invocation is unsupported or has an explicit diagnostic-module contract.

checks.question: If the step has a diagnostic module or engine source file, has the audit compared the registry row to that source file?
checks.expected_signal: Diagnostic module/source linkage is present when applicable, and absence is intentional for orchestrator-owned steps.

checks.question: Does the step use SQLite/source snapshots/central contracts where applicable and speak when falling back to JSON or filesystem reads?
checks.expected_signal: SQLite-first or declared fallback behavior is visible in source, validators or telemetry.

checks.question: Does the step report meaningful progress, degraded evidence and exceptions without noisy filler?
checks.expected_signal: Logs/telemetry/validator output explain slow, skipped, fallback or failed subwork.

checks.question: If this step changes upstream truth, do downstream validators, agent surfaces or release artifacts know when to refresh or distrust stale data?
checks.expected_signal: Freshness, lineage, dependency or proof-debt surfaces show the downstream impact.

failure_family_sweeps: If one step has undeclared artifact IO, scan all steps in the same category for missing reads_artifacts/writes_artifacts.
If one step's scheduler_class is wrong, scan SQLite-writing and mutating steps for parallel/sequential drift.
If one step lacks source linkage or telemetry, scan sibling engine/validator steps before closing the micro item.
positive_pattern_sweeps: If one step has a strong execution_contract, check sibling steps in the same category for missing scheduler_class, sqlite_writer or profile guidance.
If one step has a clear invocation_contract and diagnostic_module boundary, check sibling engine-backed steps for the same public-command/diagnostic split.
If one step reports useful telemetry or fallback honesty, check sibling long/heavy steps for equivalent non-silent reporting.
scopes.triage_rule: P0/P0.5 findings found during this micro step must be fixed before advancing the cursor when feasible. P1/P2 findings must be recorded in config/sage_work_item_registry.json before advancing.
exit_criteria: Registry row was compared to source/orchestrator behavior or explicit orchestrator-owned absence was documented.
Dependency, artifact IO, execution policy and invocation contract were checked against current generated evidence.
Failure-family and positive-pattern sibling sweeps were performed or explicitly scoped out with evidence.
P0/P0.5 fixes are closed; P1/P2 follow-ups are in the work item registry; micro cursor can advance without relying on chat memory.
New audit lessons are generalized to the reusable failure family when possible; incident-specific details are kept in evidence fields.

scopes.sample_policy: Inspect release-proof steps in contract order after pipeline-step coverage. Compare command, raw_artifact, required flag and depends_on against generated evidence.

checks.question: Does depends_on point only to upstream proof producers that must finish before this step?
checks.expected_signal: No unknown ids, cycles, artifact-name pseudo-ids or downstream finalizer prerequisites.

checks.question: Does raw_artifact match the validator or generator output, and is optional/missing evidence explicit?
checks.expected_signal: Raw artifact path exists when generated, or absence is an intentional optional/public-release gate.

checks.question: Is this proof step safe to run under its release-proof scheduling and mutating/finalizer profile?
checks.expected_signal: Mutating or environment-changing proof steps are serialized before readers.

failure_family_sweeps: If one proof step hides a stale or missing raw artifact, scan sibling proof steps that summarize or consume generated artifacts.
If one proof dependency points the wrong direction, scan all finalizer/report dependencies.
If one positive-path fixture reaches PASS through JSON or another fallback, scan sibling fixtures for authoritative-store seeding and keep degradation tests explicit.
If one aggregate consumer reports a false PASS or false UNKNOWN, scan claim-bearing consumers for local status parsing instead of the canonical evidence normalizer.
positive_pattern_sweeps: If one proof step has a precise dependency and raw artifact contract, check neighboring proof steps for the same command/raw_artifact/required clarity.
If one optional or public-release-gated proof step explains its boundary well, check sibling optional gates for equivalent explicitness.
scopes.triage_rule: P0/P0.5 release-proof contract findings must be fixed before advancing when they can affect machine readiness. P1/P2 release ergonomics or future-proofing findings must be recorded in config/sage_work_item_registry.json.
exit_criteria: Command, raw_artifact, required flag and depends_on semantics were compared to generated evidence or intentional gate status.
Failure-family and positive-pattern sibling sweeps were performed for dependency and artifact-contract drift.
Any machine-readiness blocker is closed; deferred public-release or ergonomics work is recorded centrally.

scopes.sample_policy: Inspect writer, consumer, conflict, external-input and unowned-consumer groups from the connectivity map after pipeline and release-proof contracts are checked.

checks.question: Does every consumed artifact have an owner, or is it explicitly classified as external input?
checks.expected_signal: writer_conflicts and unowned_consumed_artifacts stay empty unless explicitly justified.

checks.question: Do artifact writers and consumers expose enough lineage for downstream stale-data decisions?
checks.expected_signal: Connectivity map links writers, consumers and external inputs without hiding runtime-only assumptions.

failure_family_sweeps: If one artifact is unowned, scan nearby generator/report validators for missing artifact ownership registration.
If one external input is consumed silently, scan all external input consumers for explicit classification.
positive_pattern_sweeps: If one artifact group has clean writer/consumer/external-input classification, check sibling groups for the same explicit ownership vocabulary.
If one connectivity edge carries useful downstream stale-data context, check related artifact consumers for equivalent lineage clarity.
scopes.triage_rule: P0/P0.5 ownership/conflict findings must be fixed before advancing because they can invalidate downstream trust. P1/P2 reporting or visualization improvements must be recorded in config/sage_work_item_registry.json.
exit_criteria: Writers, consumers, conflicts, external inputs and unowned consumed artifacts were checked against system_connectivity_map.
Failure-family and positive-pattern sweeps were performed for ownership and lineage clarity.
No unowned/conflicting artifact edge remains unexplained; deferred improvements are registered centrally.

source_layer_coverage_policy.purpose: Bridge the 11 macro manual/adversarial audit layers to the 24 source-layer taxonomy so source ownership, runtime responsibility and manual review coverage do not drift apart.
source_layer_coverage_policy.rule: Every source layer in config/source_layer_taxonomy.json must have a coverage row. Critical and high-risk source layers require macro audit coverage plus source inventory/connectivity evidence before V1 sealing; medium/low layers may be inventory/connectivity checked unless a defect family pulls them into deeper review.

layers.sample_policy: Sample public entrypoints and product-facing root files when naming, CLI, release identity or packaging changes.
Sample clean install, bootstrap, dependency and mirror-sync files whenever distribution safety changes.
Sample one governing config from each changed decision domain and verify validator/release-proof consumption.
Sample schemas when artifact envelopes or generated reports change.
Sample fixtures when React claim, corpus or regression expectations change.
Sample public claim docs when release identity, claim guard or roadmap wording changes.
Inventory/connectivity check is sufficient unless historical audit text becomes release-facing evidence.
Sample shared IO, path, registry, policy, artifact and telemetry helpers when any central contract changes.
Sample SQLite state payload, source snapshot and fallback paths whenever SSOT behavior changes.
Sample target-root and project identity flows when discovery, external target or config compiler behavior changes.
Sample scheduler, orchestrator and profile policy when execution order or parallelism changes.
Sample source-to-symbol span generation and language boundaries when sequencers or Atlas/Genome contracts change.
Sample real findings against source code when audit, dead-code, circular, quality or cage logic changes.
Sample React/TS surgical findings, fixtures and claim boundaries when React intelligence changes.
Sample merge/review packets and variation boundaries when merge, task-pack or generated script behavior changes.
Sample agent-facing packets, watchdog currentness and MCP command contracts whenever this layer changes.
Sample HITL request/approval/response ledgers when seal, approval or agent-governance surfaces change.
Sample validators and release-proof dependency edges when release gates, finalizers or validation contracts change.
Sample reports when they influence product claims, health score, final suspicion, operator packet or public readiness.
Sample external target preflight and agent surfaces when external-repo behavior changes.
Sample tests/fixtures when they become release proof for a changed claim or regression family.
Sample package/runtime manifests when installation, vendoring or cross-platform runtime changes.
Sample generated/cache/output artifacts when clean mirror, retention, script generation or runtime-output policy changes.
Must remain zero or be explicitly reviewed before release sealing.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify that doctrine, policy, principle, cage and capability inputs are explicit, separated, and seal-aware.
lineage_checks: Pick one doctrine/policy rule and trace it from config to validator/release proof.
Pick one human-sealed surface and verify seal-impact status after recent changes.
adversarial_cases: Malformed or stale governance config must not become an empty PASS.
A roadmap/advisory principle must not become a V1 blocking doctrine without explicit promotion.
failure_family_sweeps: If one governance rule is duplicated locally, scan for sibling hardcoded decision domains.
If one seal-aware surface is missing from seal impact policy, scan all claim/agent/doctrine surfaces.
manual_review_prompts: Could a contributor add a new governance surface without registering validator and release proof?
Could SAGE keep running with stale human authority?
exit_criteria: Governance registry, HITL, seal impact and source contracts pass.
Any P1/P2 finding is recorded in the work item registry.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify that SAGE identifies the intended analyzed repository, MAIN project, variations and external targets without path confusion.
lineage_checks: Trace one analyzed root from discovery config to target-repo lineage artifact.
Trace one external target or variation boundary to the agent surface that consumes it.
adversarial_cases: Invalid external root must not fallback to SAGE source workspace.
Variation project must not be exposed as default MAIN edit target.
failure_family_sweeps: If one tool has ambiguous root normalization, scan MCP, watchdog and external-target entrypoints.
If one path format is platform-specific, scan agent-facing path contracts.
manual_review_prompts: Can a first-time user tell which repository SAGE is analyzing?
Can an agent open a target file using analysis_root plus repo-relative path?
exit_criteria: Target repo lineage validation passes.
Manual sample confirms path/root fields match actual filesystem.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify source files, symbols, imports and spans are captured once and carried downstream without line drift.
lineage_checks: Pick one React component and trace source file, symbol, line_start and line_end into an agent-facing packet.
Pick one Python/polyglot symbol and verify language-agnostic symbol behavior stays advisory unless supported.
Pick one SQLite-backed symbol span and verify every inspection projection preserves line, end_line and source_lines instead of downgrading to null Atlas projection fields.
Pick one incremental Atlas change and verify its project-qualified node reaches every scoped downstream consumer unchanged.
adversarial_cases: Renamed or shortened file must not keep stale old span.
Large symbol must mark partial snippet and give concrete follow-up.
A symbol span present in SQLite must not disappear when rendered through inspect_target, MCP or ContextOS agent-facing surfaces.
A non-empty Atlas must not yield a clean analyzer report when the effective project/file scope is empty.
failure_family_sweeps: If a span mismatch appears in one packet, scan all packet families that consume spans.
If a SQLite span is dropped in one projection surface, scan sibling projection and packet renderers for the same line/end_line/source_lines loss.
If one language lacks span fields, classify whether it is V1 limitation or P1/P2 roadmap debt.
If one incremental consumer loses project scope, scan every producer and consumer of changed_files and DNA change nodes.
manual_review_prompts: Can an agent edit without grep for the selected symbol?
Does source snippet match current source snapshot?
exit_criteria: Symbol/span validators pass.
Manual source-vs-packet sample matches current file.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify SQLite/source snapshot truth is preferred where applicable and JSON shadows do not regain SSOT authority.
lineage_checks: Pick one hot consumer and verify it uses SQLite/proxy before JSON fallback.
Pick one fallback path and verify it is logged as fallback, not normal truth.
Pick one undeclared large-artifact reference candidate and classify it as hot consumer, allowed metadata reference, or real violation.
adversarial_cases: Unreadable JSON must not create zero-artifact PASS.
Missing SQLite data must be explicit degraded/fallback evidence.
A proxy-loaded large artifact consumer must not remain unregistered merely because the load path is already SQLite-first.
failure_family_sweeps: If one hot path reads atlas/genome/fractal JSON first, scan all large-artifact consumers.
If one fallback is silent, scan runtime honesty and exception honesty events.
If one undeclared large-artifact candidate appears, scan sibling report and connectivity generators before closing the family.
manual_review_prompts: Is the source of truth obvious for this artifact?
Could stale JSON overwrite fresher SQLite-derived reality?
exit_criteria: SQLite-first validators pass.
Manual sample confirms fallback is visible.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify engines and cages produce evidence-backed findings without false release authority.
lineage_checks: Open one reported violation and compare rule, file and evidence against source.
Trace one engine signal to quality gate and claim boundary.
adversarial_cases: Clean repo/no violation case must not hide artifact freshness debt.
Advisory cage signal must not become release blocker unless promoted by contract.
Bare package subpath imports such as react-dom/client or zustand/react/shallow must not be classified as target-repo relative alias violations.
failure_family_sweeps: If one engine overclaims authority, scan engine_signal_contracts for sibling overclaims.
If one violation lacks actionable evidence, scan work queue and MCP packet projection.
If one slash-containing package import is misclassified as a local import, scan audit and MCP governance sibling classifiers.
manual_review_prompts: Is this finding real in source code?
Does the packet tell an agent what to change or only quote SAGE internals?
exit_criteria: Engine signal and source contracts pass.
Manual violation sample is source-grounded.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify V1 React/TypeScript surgical claim remains evidence-bounded and does not leak into unsupported universal claims.
lineage_checks: Pick one React fixture-backed rule and trace fixture, engine output and agent packet.
Pick one unsupported/roadmap React frontier signal and verify claim boundary wording.
adversarial_cases: React rule should not claim runtime proof when only static evidence exists.
Fixture PASS must not be used as universal real-world proof without corpus boundary.
failure_family_sweeps: If one React claim overstates evidence, scan release claim profiles and docs.
If one fixture mapping is stale, scan family taxonomy and fixture isolation.
manual_review_prompts: Does the React finding have enough source span for surgical action?
Is the V1 claim still scoped to React/TypeScript static governance?
exit_criteria: React chain validators pass.
Manual React sample maps to real source and fixture evidence.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify merge/variation intelligence stays review-oriented and does not confuse normal MAIN agent edit context.
lineage_checks: Pick one merge review packet and verify target, source and review-only mutation policy.
Trace one variation-only fact and verify it appears only in merge/review surfaces.
adversarial_cases: Review-only merge packet must not allow direct mutation.
Unknown target_file in merge review must explain why and what human should inspect.
failure_family_sweeps: If one merge packet lacks target clarity, scan all merge package tiers.
If variation context leaks to MAIN directive, scan all agent-facing command families.
manual_review_prompts: Could an agent accidentally edit a variation when asked to edit MAIN?
Does merge output provide enough target information for human review?
exit_criteria: Merge regression and semantic smoke pass.
Manual merge packet sample is review-only or clearly actionable.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify target-repo agent surfaces provide bounded, actionable, audience-correct context.
lineage_checks: Pick one surgical packet and trace target file, symbol, source snippet and validation command to source reality.
Pick one fail-closed packet and verify it tells the agent exactly what not to do.
Trace one ContextOS risk classification to every required dependency, blast-radius and audit input, including provenance and availability.
adversarial_cases: Packet with target_ref must include path contract or explicit usage guidance.
Partial snippet must not pretend to be full edit context.
Missing or invalid upstream risk evidence must not become zero dependents, zero violations or a low-risk action lane.
failure_family_sweeps: If one packet lacks actionability, scan all MCP command families and variants.
If one packet leaks SAGE internals to target-repo agent, scan skill and command matrix boundaries.
If one evidence aggregator treats missing input as an empty clean result, scan all decision-producing aggregators for the same false-confidence family.
manual_review_prompts: Can a new agent use this packet without knowing SAGE internals?
Can the agent complete the task with bounded context and follow-up only when needed?
exit_criteria: Agent semantic smoke and MCP surface validators pass.
Manual packet sample is source-grounded and operational.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify save-time scoped governance stays fast while preserving proof debt, unread findings and refresh guidance.
lineage_checks: Trace one changed file through watchdog pulse to session/debt artifact.
Trace one due deep-proof debt signal to agent/operator guidance.
adversarial_cases: Watchdog pulse must not imply repo-wide release proof.
Unread findings must not disappear without acknowledgement/resolution.
failure_family_sweeps: If one watchdog path defaults to host-specific root, scan all watch entrypoints.
If one pulse is silent on skipped heavy proof, scan pipeline execution profile messaging.
manual_review_prompts: Does a save-time agent know whether it should wait, refresh, or proceed?
Does watchdog preserve old unresolved findings across later saves?
exit_criteria: Watchdog freshness/stress validators pass or debt is explicit.
Manual sample shows proof debt status and recommended refresh path.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify release proof, system health, work items, audit lessons and human seal boundaries tell the same story.
lineage_checks: Trace one release blocker from source validator to system health and remaining actions.
Trace one closed/manual lesson to audit lesson registry and release proof coverage.
Trace one release-proof dependency chain and verify it points from upstream validator to downstream finalizer without a reverse edge.
adversarial_cases: Machine READY must not become human SEALED automatically.
Existing human seal must become review/reseal-required after protected changes.
Historical human seal evidence must not be summarized as effective current seal after protected changes.
An early registry or contract validator must not depend on system health, final suspicion, artifact alignment, or remaining-action finalizers that consume its output.
failure_family_sweeps: If one blocker appears in one report but not another, scan release health/remaining/final audit consumers.
If one report exposes only historical human seal status, scan all release-facing consumers for missing effective human seal status.
If one lesson is not linked to guard/work item/roadmap, scan all audit lesson rows.
If one release-proof dependency points to a downstream finalizer, scan all release-proof dependency edges for unknown ids, artifact-name ids and cycles.
manual_review_prompts: Do machine verdict, public release readiness and human seal status remain separate?
Are all deferred P1/P2 findings visible outside chat?
exit_criteria: Release closure validators pass.
Only expected human reseal/clean-install proof remains before public release.

audit_layers.purpose: Verify clean distribution is a reproducible package, not contaminated by runtime output or source-only state.
lineage_checks: Trace one synced source file from source SAGE to clean mirror.
Trace one runtime output generated by validation and confirm it is cleaned from mirror.
adversarial_cases: Cleaner must not run destructively against active source workspace.
Clean mirror validation must not pass with output/cache artifacts present.
failure_family_sweeps: If one generated artifact leaks into mirror, scan all runtime-output retention and clean-sync filters.
If one entrypoint works only on Windows, scan install/doctor/CLI commands for cross-platform assumptions.
manual_review_prompts: Could a new user install and run without hidden local machine assumptions?
Is clean mirror free of source runtime artifacts after validation?
exit_criteria: Clean distribution validation passes after cleanup.
Final external clean install proof is requested only after V1 seal closure.
